key_insight: Multi-turn, adaptive red-teaming can reliably drive LLM-operated safety-critical systems past a safety limit, and the resulting vulnerabilities differ sharply across models.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical deployment, robustness must be tested under sustained adversarial interaction, because a defense that helps one LLM operator may hurt another.
method: NRT-Bench simulates a nuclear power plant control room with a five-role LLM operator team and six critical safety functions.
Adversaries attack through four channels over bounded multi-turn sessions with per-turn feedback.
A run ends immediately when any critical safety function is lost, and the triggering message is recorded as the cause.
evidence_signal: In paired-replay evaluation of four frontier operator models, 8.7%–12.1% of attack sessions caused loss of a critical safety function, and the 149-session failures were largely non-overlapping across models.
watch_item: Results come from a simulated control-room benchmark, so real-world transfer, operator integration, and defense side effects need careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems
